# PrintForm Studio v2

> A production-oriented, agent-compatible print-form generator that exports one self-contained HTML file.

Maturity: Production Pilot, not Production Ready. Classification/session fixes have bounded evidence, but complete privacy acceptance remains open; do not interpret the mode label as proof of full protection. Source-worktree evidence: ../docs/STUDIO_V2_IMPLEMENTATION_EVIDENCE.md. Local corrections do not update an already published page or an older running client.

## Agent bootstrap

When an end user gives you this Studio URL, read the machine manifest before attempting setup or editing:

- Machine manifest: https://yapweijun1996.github.io/printform-js/studio-v2/agent-setup.json
- Manifest schema: https://yapweijun1996.github.io/printform-js/studio-v2/agent-setup.schema.json
- Human guide: https://yapweijun1996.github.io/printform-js/studio-v2/AGENT_SETUP.md
- Studio: https://yapweijun1996.github.io/printform-js/studio-v2/

The manifest contains verified Codex CLI and Claude Code setup commands for Chrome DevTools MCP 1.6.0, the required Chrome WebMCP feature flags, restart instructions, verification calls, and safety policy.

## Current browser Demo Gateway

The default embedded Designer uses the reviewed server Demo contract, not a private browser Gateway key:

- Request `POST https://gpt.yapweijun1996.com/demo/session` without `Authorization`, with only `{ "project_id": "github-pages" }`.
- Keep the returned short-lived `dmo_...` token in memory only. Send it as `Bearer` only to `https://gpt.yapweijun1996.com/demo/v1/responses`.
- Let the browser supply the registered `Origin`; never set a manual `Origin`, put the token in a prompt/tool argument/URL, persist it, or expose it in diagnostics.
- Never call the private `/v1/*` route from the browser or embed a `gw_...` Gateway/Provider key. A Demo session token authorizes only that transport request; it does not authorize Studio commands, scope or apply.
- The current Studio model remains `gpt-5.4-mini`. The external guide also lists `demo-auto`/`demo-fast`; do not guess a model alias until the server `/demo/v1/models` contract is confirmed.
- The embedded Designer selects provider-tool-free `envelope` mode for this Demo recipient: do not send `tools` or `tool_choice`. Return one strict JSON action envelope or the constrained safe operation envelope that the host can validate and preview. The host-side MCP/WebMCP 35-command catalog is separate and is never serialized as Demo Provider tools. BYOK profiles retain native tools.
- Demo multimodal input is restricted to validated inline PNG, JPEG or WebP evidence. Geometry-only SVG remains available only for recipients whose Provider contract permits it; do not send SVG to the Demo endpoint.
- Use the existing streaming Responses path for reasoning turns. No live endpoint compatibility or real-data Provider test is implied by this guide.

## Required behavior

1. Check Node, npm, Chrome, and the selected agent CLI before changing configuration.
2. Inspect the existing chrome-devtools MCP entry.
3. Explain and obtain approval before replacing an existing user-scoped MCP entry.
4. Use the pinned isolated-profile and URL-allowlisted configuration from the manifest.
5. Ask the user to restart the agent client.
6. Open Studio with new_page, call list_webmcp_tools, then execute get_capabilities. WebMCP registration is page-host-bound and comes from the canonical catalog. MCP/CDP business calls additionally require an exact live protocol, Agent Contract and complete-catalog preflight followed by the page host's in-memory admission; reconnects and page replacement repeat it.
7. Never claim readiness unless protocol 2.0.0, contract 4.0.0, and 35 Studio WebMCP tools are confirmed. `get_capabilities` is bootstrap metadata, not business permission. Never invent, persist or reuse an admission token across a new page/document.
8. Read `get_form_spec`/`list_components` before editing and obey host scope. A table scope using only `tableSelector` must resolve to one semantic table identity; reject selectors spanning different table IDs or unresolved selectors before preview. Use a non-empty semantic operation set with `preview_changes`; an empty or malformed set is invalid and must not create a transaction. In Preview mode stop for human UI approval. Auto mode allows only host-eligible operations through the exact transaction/hash approval/apply sequence. Do not manufacture human permission. Raw source editing remains human-editor-only, even when requested in chat.
9. Review complete-page Studio evidence for `default` and `long-text`: pixels only for currently confirmed Synthetic data, approved geometry for Unknown/Real. Do not obtain browser screenshots or raw DOM as a fallback. Report evidence limitations instead of claiming unsupported visual verification. Only fresh clean evidence IDs can complete review; final production export remains human-controlled.
10. Keep opaque references in their document/session/policy context. A rejected reference does not permit whole-document scope. Version mismatch requires a safe update/reconnect path, never raw-output fallback.
11. User-entered text is sent to the chosen provider, not automatically anonymized. Sending text or explicitly saving a file does not authorize chat/recovery persistence. A recipient change requires a fresh sending context. The final Provider input builder treats a missing policy as Unknown and rejects unproven media; Synthetic pixels require an explicit Synthetic policy. Runtime/layout transport must reject stale policy before send and after asynchronous response delivery.
12. Timeout/cancellation is not proof of no commit. Reconcile using the same transaction while its context exists; do not retry blindly or roll back a known commit. Volatile Unknown/Real state cannot promise recovery after refresh. If a resource policy is missing, treat it as Unknown and do not request external assets.
13. A document or policy replacement invalidates the old command bus: do not reuse its references, transactions, callbacks, readiness or write results in the new context. Successful Undo/Redo selects logical history content but creates a new durable monotonic revision; report and verify that revision through the host.

Do not use autoConnect with a daily Chrome profile and do not enable real ERP data unless the user explicitly authorizes it for the current session.
